opening.argument: The segment presents an Apple-support impersonation as a warning, not as an offer to obtain money. It reports that a woman was told to buy gift cards for supposed MacBook assistance, then states that she gave the caller $800 before realizing the number was not really Apple. The purpose is expressly protective: she wants to warn other Apple users, and the report tells viewers, "So don't do it and don't waste your money." Its visual presentation reinforces that framing through a "DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY" banner and the headline "WOMAN TARGETED BY APPLE SUPPORT SCAM." The segment therefore explains the payment demand and cautions viewers against complying with it.

citations.quote: She ended up giving him $800 worth of iTunes gift cards before she realized the Apple support number she called wasn't really Apple.
Now she just wants to warn other Apple users. So that they don't lose hundreds of dollars like she did.
So don't do it and don't waste your money.
